summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma s/p TACE and RFA, and chronic depression was admitted due to hypokalemia and decompensated depression following her daughter's metastatic breast cancer diagnosis. She presented with a potassium level of 2.6 mEq/L, likely due to recent non-compliance with spironolactone, and mild hepatic encephalopathy with asterixis and AAOx2. She was started on IV and oral potassium, resumed her home dose of spironolactone, and given a short course of intensified lactulose before returning to her baseline regimen. Psychiatry recommended discontinuing trazodone and zolpidem due to risk of confusion. Her potassium normalized, mental status remained at her clinical baseline, and labs showed stable liver function and pancytopenia. Blood cultures were negative. She was discharged home with support services, continuing all home medications except the discontinued sedatives, and plans for outpatient follow-up with psychiatry, social work, and her liver team.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
